2607.05316.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
2607.05316.paper_summary: Large language models generate one token at a time, yet their responses show remarkably consistent length structure: step-by-step solutions converge in predictable token counts, retrievals stop after a few sentences, retractions extend responses by measurable amounts. We ask whether the model carries an internal estimate of how much response remains. Training minimal-capacity linear probes on frozen hidden states of three open-weight 7-8B models across seven completion-style datasets, we find three converging pieces of evidence. First, total response length is linearly decodable from the prompt's last hidden state alone, before any output is emitted. Second, probe directions trained on natural-language datasets transfer broadly, including to controlled synthetic completions never seen in training, outperforming a statistical baseline; the converse direction generally fails, and this asymmetry is itself informative. Third, on curated high-loss completions, the probe's per-position estimate shifts upward at the moment the model retracts and restarts a partial solution, a directional behavior no position-only predictor can reproduce (qualitative, not aggregate). We frame this as approximate estimation of remaining generation length, distinct from exact-counting impossibility results for transformers, and interpret it as evidence that LLMs maintain a plan-like internal representation of output length (decodable, not necessarily used causally).
2607.05316.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型一次生成一個標記，但它們的回應顯示出顯著一致的長度結構：逐步解決方案在可預測的標記數量上收斂，檢索在幾句話後停止，撤回則使回應延長了可測量的量。我們詢問模型是否擁有對剩餘回應量的內部估計。在三個開放權重的7-8B模型上，對七個完成風格數據集的凍結隱藏狀態訓練最小容量的線性探針，我們發現三個收斂的證據。首先，總回應長度可以僅從提示的最後隱藏狀態線性解碼，這在任何輸出發出之前。其次，對自然語言數據集訓練的探針方向廣泛轉移，包括對訓練中從未見過的受控合成完成，超越了統計基準；相反的方向通常失敗，而這種不對稱性本身就是有信息的。第三，在精心策劃的高損失完成中，探針的每個位置估計在模型撤回並重新啟動部分解決方案的瞬間向上移動，這種方向行為是任何僅基於位置的預測器無法重現的（質性，而非總體）。我們將此框架視為對剩餘生成長度的近似估計，與Transformer的精確計數不可能結果不同，並解釋為證據，表明LLMs維持一種類似計劃的內部輸出長度表示（可解碼，但不一定被因果使用）。
